items.title: Nvidia Stock Plunges After Jensen Huang Resigns as CEO
items.summary: News that the chipmaker’s chief executive, Jensen Huang, resigned drove Nvidia’s stock down, though the broader market rose slightly.

items.title: Who Is Colette Kress, the Interim Nvidia CEO Replacing Jensen Huang?
items.summary: Ms. Kress, the company’s chief financial officer, joined Nvidia in 2013.

items.title: Singapore Says US Not Helpful on Investigation Into Alice Huang and Megaspeed
items.summary: In a statement, Singapore said it held Alice Huang’s passport months after President Trump was briefed that she was a spy.

items.title: Excavation Was Taking Place Next to Building in Brooklyn That Collapsed
items.summary: New York City officials had ordered work at the construction site to stop after an apartment building in the Flatbush neighborhood collapsed onto it.

items.title: What to Know About the Deadly Building Collapse in Brooklyn
items.summary: At least eight people were killed and more than a dozen others injured when a three-story building in Flatbush collapsed, officials said.

items.title: Trump Says He’s Pulling Vance Off Iran Talks to Focus on Fraud Campaign
items.summary: The announcement on social media deepened questions about what the president’s plan is to end the war. “We don’t need a deal with Iran,” he wrote.

items.title: Kennedy’s Future: Will Democrats Try to Impeach Him, or Actually Work With Him?
items.summary: Most Democrats abhor the health secretary’s stance on vaccines, but some see an opportunity to win voters from his MAHA movement by joining with him on food and environmental issues.

items.title: Democrats Put Targets on Notice as Trump Oversight Takes Shape
items.summary: Letters sent by two key House committees tell companies and officials not to destroy documents.

items.title: Will the Supreme Court Thwart Congressional Investigations?
items.summary: Lawmakers must dodge rulings on immunity, standing and “valid legislative purpose.”

items.title: Democrats Unite on Economic Populism After Midterm Victories
items.summary: Moderate Democrats and progressives have long feuded over who should drive their party’s economic agenda. But many newly elected members say they share the same big goals.

items.title: Casualties continue to rise after Brooklyn building collapses
items.summary: First responders continue to search for survivors after a building in Brooklyn collapsed, leaving at least eight dead and dozens injured.

items.title: Democrats want to stop Trump's arch, golf course and more. What are their options?
items.summary: As Trump's arch and other projects make their way through the courts, many critics are looking to Congress to stop them. Democrats have a few tools, including funding and oversight.

items.title: The SS United States takes its final voyage to the bottom of the Gulf of Mexico
items.summary: A ship bigger than the Titanic is being sunk off the coast of Florida to make an artificial reef.

items.title: D.C. shooting leaves 1 person killed, 4 injured. Gunman dead
items.summary: A gunman opened fire at a gym in Washington, D.C.'s Logan Circle Thursday morning. One person has been confirmed killed and four others injured. The gunman is dead, according to police.

items.title: U.S. envoys meet with Putin in the Kremlin after Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi
items.summary: Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff went to the Kremlin to brief Russian President Vladimir Putin and are scheduled to fly later to Ireland for talks with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy.

items.title: Indonesia's VP resigns as his eligibility and academic credentials are questioned
items.summary: Raka is the son of former President Joko Widodo. The Constitutional Court and the Supreme Court ruled last month that the documents that Raka submitted regarding his overseas education didn't meet election requirements.

items.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang steps down amid alleged spy scandal
items.summary: Huang co-founded the chipmaker Nvidia, which has become one of the driving forces behind the AI boom. But reports that he may have had an affair with an alleged Chinese spy quickly sank his career.

items.title: Colom wins Mississippi Senate race. And, White House warns Dems over future probes
items.summary: After more than a week of counting ballots, Scott Colom has narrowly won the Mississippi Senate seat. And, the White House has sent a letter warning Democrats who plan to investigate the administration.

items.title: A blue wave helped offset for now a falling tally of Black members in the U.S. House
items.summary: A Supreme Court ruling that further weakened the Voting Rights Act paved the way for a record drop in Black representation in Congress. But a midterm blue wave helped hold off such a decline for now.

items.title: At least 23 states considered laws governing ICE and schools this year
items.summary: When ICE agents show up at a school, educators rely on a patchwork of policies to know what to do. This year, many state legislatures tried to update those policies.

items.title: San Francisco approves first gay bathhouse since AIDS epidemic
items.summary: San Fransisco had as many as 20 gay bathhouses at their peak in 1982. Today there are none, but that may change soon.

items.title: Home sales in worst slump since the aftermath of the Great Recession
items.summary: Home sales are slumping, and mortgage rates have pushed up the typical monthly payment for homebuyers in the U.S.

items.title: Eight dead and at least 18 injured after Brooklyn building collapse
items.summary: A rescue operation continued Thursday as first responders sought anyone trapped beneath the rubble.

items.title: What new prostate cancer recommendations say about who should get blood tests
items.summary: The American Cancer Society’s first update to prostate cancer screening guidance in more than a decade endorsed regular PSA tests for certain older men.

items.title: College students with disabilities may soon face less red tape
items.summary: A bipartisan bill making its way through Congress aims to smooth the transition into college and to help students qualify for accommodations without additional testing.

items.title: Which generation has had it easiest for homebuying? New research shows a shift.
items.summary: Millennials had a better housing market than boomers. An analysis shows how the economic shifts of recent years have changed that.

items.title: Drunk raccoon’s boozy night has helped raise $290K for an animal shelter
items.summary: “I don’t know when we’ve owed a debt of gratitude to any animal as much as we do to that raccoon,” said Faye Prichard, Hanover County board supervisor.

items.title: Opioid settlement money is helping fight homelessness. Some fear blurred lines.
items.summary: Millions from recent legal settlements are being spent on homelessness and housing, raising questions about whether the funds are staying focused on addiction.

items.title: Not all sports help the brain in the same way. This is what may be best for ADHD.
items.summary: Researchers found differences in the effects of running, martial arts and more.

items.title: Richard Posner, influential and iconoclastic federal judge, dies at 87
items.summary: He served nearly 36 years on the U.S. Court of Appeals for the 7th Circuit in Chicago and was ranked by many as second in influence only to members of the Supreme Court.
